metadata.goal: Analyze the given vessel trajectories and summarize the typical routes in this part of the Kattegat, together with their traffic characteristics.
metadata.category: Kattegat route structure and transverse traffic distribution
metadata.header: Kattegat A/B/E Route Structure and Lane Displacement
metadata.dataset_description: This derived case contains 47 AIS-like vessel trajectories in the Kattegat area, static vessel attributes, and directional reference-lane geometry for historical-style Routes A, B, and E. The trajectory table intentionally does not expose route assignments. Its A/B/E topology is derived from the official-transit-route layout in Figure 9-2 and the route descriptions in Sections 9.1–9.2 of risk_to_ship_traffic.pdf; vessel-type proportions and the directional transverse-distribution pattern follow the Chapter 9 route-analysis findings.
metadata.source_note: The current 2026 AIS sample confirms Kattegat Cargo, Tanker, and Passenger traffic. Official A/B/E labels and lane geometries are not present in raw AIS, so the Figure 9-2-style reference lanes are provided for this analysis case.

insight_list.insight: Three recurrent bidirectional traffic corridors structure the selected Kattegat area: Route A follows a southwest–northeast corridor southeast of Anholt, Route B is a northwest–southeast cross-Kattegat corridor west of Anholt, and Route E follows a southwest–northeast corridor on the western side of the project area.

routes.E: SW–NE west of the project area

plot.title: Three Recurrent Kattegat Traffic Corridors
plot.description: Observed trajectories form three route families around Anholt. Dashed lines are the supplied directional reference-lane centrelines; route labels are not attached to trajectory points.

insight_list.question: What recurrent route corridors can be identified from the trajectory geometry and directional route-reference lanes in the selected Kattegat area?
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path
points = pd.read_csv(dataset_path)
lanes = pd.read_csv(Path('route_lanes.csv'))
print(points.groupby('trajectory_id').agg(vessel_id=('vessel_id','first'), start_time=('timestamp','min'), mean_cog=('cog','mean')))
for route, g in lanes.groupby('route_name'):
    plt.plot(g['lon'], g['lat'], '.', ms=2, label=f'Route {route} reference')
plt.scatter(points['lon'], points['lat'], s=1, alpha=.15)
plt.legend(); plt.axis('equal'); plt.show()

insight_list.insight: Route A is tanker-dominated, with 12 of its 18 vessel trajectories classified as Tanker (67%). Cargo traffic is most pronounced on Route B (11 of 15 trajectories, 73%) and Route E (8 of 14 trajectories, 57%).

insight_list.question: After assigning trajectories to the three route corridors, how does vessel-type composition differ between Route A, Route B, and Route E?
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
points = pd.read_csv(dataset_path)
vessels = pd.read_csv(user_dataset_path)
lanes = pd.read_csv(Path('route_lanes.csv'))
tracks = points.groupby('trajectory_id').agg(vessel_id=('vessel_id','first'), mean_lon=('lon','mean'), mean_lat=('lat','mean'), mean_cog=('cog','mean')).reset_index()
# Assign each track to the nearest compatible directional reference lane before merging vessel types.
print(tracks.merge(vessels[['vessel_id','ship_type']], on='vessel_id').groupby('ship_type').size())

insights: Three recurrent bidirectional traffic corridors structure the selected Kattegat area: Route A follows a southwest–northeast corridor southeast of Anholt, Route B is a northwest–southeast cross-Kattegat corridor west of Anholt, and Route E follows a southwest–northeast corridor on the western side of the project area.

Route A is tanker-dominated, with 12 of its 18 vessel trajectories classified as Tanker (67%). Cargo traffic is most pronounced on Route B (11 of 15 trajectories, 73%) and Route E (8 of 14 trajectories, 57%).
For all three route families, directional-lane track positions are not symmetric around their nominal lane centres.
summary: Traffic in the selected Kattegat area is organized around three recurring official-style bidirectional corridors. Their vessel composition differs clearly: Route A is tanker-dominated, whereas cargo traffic is more prominent on Routes B and E. Across the corridors, vessels also favour the outer side of their directional lane instead of being centred symmetrically between opposing flows.
